The fit gives **Dq ≈ 3 340 cm⁻¹** and **B ≈ 740 cm⁻¹**, with C ≈ 3 250 cm⁻¹ (= 4.4 B).

**Method.** I fitted the three bands to the low-spin d⁵ Tanabe–Sugano manifold, pinned to the low-spin ²T₂g ground term, using `ts_fit_spectrum`. The tool's default C (3 850 cm⁻¹) implies C/B ≈ 4, not 4.4, so I held C fixed at several trial values and iterated until C/B was consistent.

| Trial C (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | C/B | RMS residual (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 850 (default) | 960 | 3 142 | 4.0 | 106 |
| 3 700 | 738 | 3 375 | 5.0 | 8 |
| 3 240 | 739 | 3 342 | 4.38 | 1.2 |
| 3 000 | 740 | 3 325 | 4.05 | 2.4 |

At C = 3 240 cm⁻¹ the fit reproduces the observed maxima to about 1 cm⁻¹ and gives C/B ≈ 4.38. Setting C exactly to 4.4 B moves B by well under 1%, so B ≈ 739–740 cm⁻¹ and Dq ≈ 3 340 cm⁻¹.

The Dq value is the fitted one at C ≈ 3 240 cm⁻¹. Since 10Dq ≈ 33 400 cm⁻¹ is well above the three observed bands, the fit assigns them to the low-spin ²T₂g → ²A₂, ²T₁ and ²T₂ transitions, with the 29 360 and 29 620 cm⁻¹ bands close together. The fit is a model-based estimate, not an independent measurement.
